discovery: Atom interferometry: development of matter-wave interferometers with atoms and their use for precision measurement of inertial forces and fundamental constants

nominees.name: Christian J. Bordé
nominees.affiliation: LNE-SYRTE, Observatoire de Paris, and Laboratoire de Physique des Lasers, Université Paris 13, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: In 1991 three approaches turned the matter-wave thought experiment into working instruments. Bordé showed that light-pulse Ramsey spectroscopy forms an atom interferometer. Pritchard built the first interferometer for atoms using nanofabricated gratings. Kasevich, working with Chu, demonstrated light-pulse interferometry with stimulated Raman transitions. Their atom interferometers now measure gravity, rotation and gravity gradients with sensitivity that rivals or beats classical instruments. They supply the most precise determinations of the fine-structure constant and h/m, which test QED and the Standard Model at the sub-ppb level. They have measured Newton's G, tested the equivalence principle at the 10^-12 level, constrained dark-energy models, and underpin proposals for gravitational-wave detection and quantum tests of gravity. Field gravimeters and inertial navigation show the technology's practical value. Few experimental inventions have opened so many new measurement capabilities, each backed by a rigorous error budget.
